title: Token econ — solo scratchpad
content:
High-level goals / constraints (reminder):
- Keep entry simple for PLG: single, predictable bill for early users.
- Expose clear levers for power users (batching, quantization, dedicated).
- Make Dedicated/Private upsell obvious when unit econ improves at scale.

Notes to self: rough assumptions to sanity-check pricing buckets. These are purposely conservative for now. Will iterate once I get real infra numbers from infra-costs-2026 sheet.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- GPU amortized serving cost per 1M generated tokens (total cost, infra + infra ops + overhead): $45 — corresponds to moderate batching, mix of gpus.
- Embedding compute (per 1M tokens processed for embedding): $12 (smaller model, vector ops).
- Storage + KVS/cache + network per 1M tokens: $2.
- Support/monitoring/other overhead allocation per 1M tokens: $6.
- Effective total cost per 1M tokens (gen path): $55.
- Assume average prompt: 150 ctx tokens in, 350 gen tokens out => 500 tokens total per request.

Unit math examples:
- Per-request cost: 500 tokens => 0.0005 of M-token. Cost = 0.0005 * $55 = $0.0275 (2.75 cents) per average request (gen path).
- Equivalent per-1k-tokens price given cost: $55 / 1000 = $0.055 per 1k tokens. (Note: this is cost, we should price above this for margin.)

Pricing sketch (PLG-friendly tiers):
- Free tier: 100k tokens / month (context+gen) — frictionless for toy apps.
- Starter: $9 / month -> 2M tokens included -> effective included cost to us = 2 * $55 = $110 (ouch). So Starter price massively below cost. Need to rethink.
  - Conclusion: cannot give 2M tokens for $9 with these cost assumptions. Starter should be 200k tokens or reduce assumed cost by enabling aggressive cold-cache throttles / lower model.

Threshold model idea (mix of seat & usage):
- Seats (account-level analytics, support) + usage pricing to avoid heavy free-tier abuse.
- Example: $10 seat / month + $0.02 per 1k tokens beyond included allowance.
  - With 500-token avg request, $0.02 per 1k = $0.00001 per token => per-request = 500 * 0.00001 = $0.005 => 0.5 cents; margin if our cost per 1k = $0.055, so $0.02 yields big loss. So price must be > $0.065 per 1k to be profitable with current cost.

Simple per-1k slab that would cover costs + margin: (target 50% gross margin)
- Cost per 1k tokens = $0.055. Price target = $0.11 per 1k.
- Offer 3 tiers:
  - Developer: $15/mo, 150k tokens included, $0.12 per 1k overage
  - Team: $150/mo, 2M tokens included, $0.10 per 1k overage
  - Business: custom pricing, committed capacity (discounts for reserved Dedicated), SLA

But these numbers conflict with PLG expectations (users expect $0.02-$0.06 per 1k). To bridge: need to reduce cost assumptions via: more batching, kv/prefix caching, smaller cheaper models as default, or offer limited output size.

Cost reduction levers to model before finalizing pricing:
- Default model family: use smaller quantized model for free/Starter requests (e.g., 4-bit LlamaX) — assume cost reduction 3x (-> cost per 1M tokens $18)
- Intelligent routing: route low-tier to cheaper regions/hardware when latency not required -> 1.2x reduction on average
- Cache hit rate for repetitive prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples): assume 20% hit -> cost drop proportional to generation tokens
- Batching improvements: increase average batch size from 8 -> 24 -> approx 1.6x efficiency on throughput ops.

If we apply combined 4x reduction for starter workload, cost per 1k ~ $0.055 / 4 = $0.01375 -> price $0.03 per 1k could be viable with 50% margin on that segment.

Edge cases & tricky charges:
- Embeddings pricing: usually sold separately (per vector). Recommend: price embeddings per 1k input tokens processed OR per-vector depending on downstream. Quick rule: $0.006 per 1k tokens for embeddings (aiming margin against $12 per 1M tokens -> $0.012 per 1k cost).
- Context-heavy apps (long documents / retrieval-heavy): charge for context tokens explicitly and consider a cheaper per-context token rate vs generation token rate.
- Function/tool calling: charge per call (small flat) or include in token accounting? Best to include tokens but separate metric in billing UI for transparency.

Dedicated upsell / reserved capacity pricing:
- Offer committed monthly $/GPU-hour or $/M-token discounts (e.g., 40–60% off hosted list) in exchange for commit.
- Example: If hosted list price per 1k = $0.11, Dedicated commit at 50% -> $0.055 per 1k. This must still leave room for margin relative to Dedicated cost basis (lower infra ops per token).

Quick scenarios (sanity):
1) Small PLG app: 1000 monthly requests * 500 tokens = 500k tokens -> If priced at $0.12 per 1k => bill = 0.5 * $0.12 = $0.06/month (tiny). Good onboarding. But this assumes avg tokens smaller; verify.
2) Mid startup: 1M requests * 200 tokens = 200M tokens -> cost to us at $55/M = $11k; price at $0.11/1k -> revenue $22k -> margin ~$11k -> Dedicated/commit conversation triggered.

Open questions to resolve with infra/costs team: (action items)
- Get real amortized cost numbers per model family / quantization level / region. (Jira PRIC-2026 assigned)
- Break out costs into: warmup/latency penalty (small short requests cost more) vs steady-state throughput.
- Cache hit empirical rates from production (how often do users reuse system prompts).
- Cost delta for streaming vs non-streaming requests.
- GPU reservation and pre-warm cost per slot (affects smallest tenant economics).

UX notes / billing design thoughts:
- Show token estimates in Console along with cost estimate ("Your last 30 days: 1.2M tokens -> est $X").
- Allow customers to set hard token caps with auto-fail-mode or soft alerts.
- Show per-call breakdown sample to help users optimize prompts (pins for batch-friendly vs chat-heavy).

Scratch ideas for promo / intro offers:
- "Starter credit" as compute time rather than token count (reduces abuse if cold-start expensive).
- Time-limited free access to higher-performance models (to demonstrate quality upgrade path).

Quick to-do (my next 48h):
- Pull infra cost per model family (ask @Liam O'Neill)
- Draft two concrete starter bundles that preserve margin (one conservative, one aggressive)
- Mock billing UI screenshots — show included tokens, per-1k price, and estimated monthly cost based on sample traffic

Random scraps / heuristics I like:
- Price per 1k anchored to a small integer (0.01 / 0.03 / 0.09) — easier to communicate.
- Make embeddings a separate line-item in UI: "Vectors used / month".
- When in doubt, bias towards predictable pricing for PLG. Users hate opaque overage surprises.

End of scratchpad.

Unresolved: how to reconcile PLG expectations with our current per-token cost math without sacrificing margins. Need real infra numbers to finalize.
